body:
## Problem

Plugins can load buffers during `BufAdd`, suppressing normal filetype detection. After `:restart` restores the session, those buffers may have an empty `filetype`, preventing filetype-dependent setup such as Treesitter highlighting from attaching.

## Solution

After loading the restart session, re-run filetype detection for loaded buffers with an empty `filetype`.

comment_regular_data.body: @justinmk I'll merge once I get your blessing :)

thank you for making restart more reliable :) i am curious why this only affects restart though, i.e. i would expect the solution to live in the session logic, not restart-specific. if there is a reason for this, would be helpful if the commit msg explains it.
this patch https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41711#issuecomment-5553660022 seems interesting, and related, though I'm not sure if both changes are needed.

> thank you for making restart more reliable :) i am curious why this only affects restart though, i.e. i would expect the solution to live in the session logic, not restart-specific. if there is a reason for this, would be helpful if the commit msg explains it.

Good point. There is no particular reason for this to be `restart`-specific. I put the workaround there because `restart` has an explicit post-session-load step, but the underlying failure can happen during any session restore if a `BufAdd` handler loads a buffer before it is edited.

@justinmk are you okay with merging this as is or do you want me to refactor it into a more general solution? FWIW I don't think https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41711 it's exactly the same issue.

> FWIW I don't think #41711 it's exactly the same issue.

so this doesn't close it?

I'm eager to make :restart work better, but this PR as-is seems to treat a very specific symptom (which doesn't seem to affect me...), and we could easily forget to remove `_restore_filetypes_after_restart` later once the root cause is fixed.

What plugin/filetype is having this symptom for you?

> > FWIW I don't think https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41711 it's exactly the same issue.

> so this doesn't close it?

I tested this PR and it doesn't close 41711.

41711 is explicitly hampered by a combination of `ex_doautoall()` setting `b_did_filetype = true` and then `ex_setfiletype()` returning early when that flag is set. But the problem is that even though that flag is set, when restarting the first buffer doesn't have a filetype set yet, so the autocmd in `filetype.lua` never takes effect because `setf` just returns early. 

I believe for 41711, an explicit safeguard about buffer filetype being empty or not in the conditional check to return early in `ex_setfiletype()` is necessary. After all that command should set the filetype and not return early solely relying on if `b_did_filetype` is `true`.
Thanks @dpetka2001 for your references / analysis in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41711#issuecomment-5553660022 . Trying your patch in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41958

Is it correct to frame the general problem as: "filetype detection doesn't work if buffer-load has nested events blocked" ?

Affects:
- `nvim -S`
- `:source <session>` (and thus `:restart`)
- any plugin doing `bufload()` from a non-nested autocmd

For reference here's an alternative more general patch (I haven't tested it yet):


<details>
<summary>Patch</summary>


```diff
diff --git i/src/nvim/fileio.c w/src/nvim/fileio.c
index 0b04f0302c8a..0366b444a56a 100644
--- i/src/nvim/fileio.c
+++ w/src/nvim/fileio.c
@@ -1915,13 +1915,20 @@ failed:
       apply_autocmds_exarg(EVENT_FILTERREADPOST, NULL, sfname,
                            false, curbuf, eap);
     } else if (newfile || (read_buffer && sfname != NULL)) {
-      apply_autocmds_exarg(EVENT_BUFREADPOST, NULL, sfname,
-                           false, curbuf, eap);
+      bool did_bufreadpost = apply_autocmds_exarg(EVENT_BUFREADPOST, NULL, sfname,
+                                                  false, curbuf, eap);
       if (!curbuf->b_au_did_filetype && *curbuf->b_p_ft != NUL) {
         // EVENT_FILETYPE was not triggered but the buffer already has a
         // filetype.  Trigger EVENT_FILETYPE using the existing filetype.
         apply_autocmds(EVENT_FILETYPE, curbuf->b_p_ft, curbuf->b_fname, true, curbuf);
       }
+      if (!did_bufreadpost && *curbuf->b_p_ft == NUL && augroup_exists("filetypedetect")) {
+        // A non-nested autocommand loading this buffer (e.g. bufload() from BufAdd) skips
+        // BufReadPost, thus 'filetype' detection.  Detect now, else 'filetype' stays empty: the
+        // file is not read again when the buffer is later entered.
+        apply_autocmds_group(EVENT_BUFREADPOST, sfname, NULL, true, augroup_find("filetypedetect"),
+                             curbuf, curwin, NULL, NULL, false);
+      }
     } else {
       apply_autocmds_exarg(EVENT_FILEREADPOST, sfname, sfname,
                            false, NULL, eap);
diff --git i/test/functional/autocmd/filetype_spec.lua w/test/functional/autocmd/filetype_spec.lua
index 191447732931..a98bad6db7f4 100644
--- i/test/functional/autocmd/filetype_spec.lua
+++ w/test/functional/autocmd/filetype_spec.lua
@@ -29,4 +29,25 @@ describe('autocmd FileType', function()
     command('doautocmd User X')
     t.eq('markdown', eval('&filetype'))
   end)
+
+  it('detected when an autocmd loads the buffer with autocmds blocked #41663', function()
+    local file = t.tmpname(false) .. '.md'
+    t.write_file(file, '# hi\n')
+    command('filetype on')
+    -- BufAdd is deferred, so bufload() runs from an autocmd: the read skips BufReadPost, and the
+    -- later :edit does not read the file again.
+    t.eq(
+      'markdown',
+      n.exec_lua(function(f)
+        vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('BufAdd', {
+          callback = function(ev)
+            vim.fn.bufload(ev.buf)
+          end,
+        })
+        local buf = vim.fn.bufadd(f)
+        vim.cmd('edit ' .. vim.fn.fnameescape(f))
+        return vim.bo[buf].filetype
+      end, file)
+    )
+  end)
 end)
```

</details>
